ops.title: In colocated jj+git, deleting a git branch (e.g. an agent worktree branch) whose ancestry includes unpushed bookmark-less main-chain commits makes jj's next import ABANDON those commits and rebase descendants into conflicts

ops.body:
2026-07-08, cc-pool repo (colocated jj+git): after harvesting an agent worktree's commits via `git cherry-pick -n` + `jj commit`, running `git branch -D worktree-agent-*` abandoned two commits from MY working-copy chain (the substrate + a fix) because they (a) were in the deleted branch's git ancestry (the worktree had been created from then-HEAD) and (b) sat under no jj bookmark — only reachable as @'s ancestors, which the import's reachability pass did not honor. jj rebased the surviving descendants onto main → (conflict) commits whose git export was a ~355k-line materialized-conflict tree.

**Why:** agent worktrees branch from current git HEAD, so a worktree branch's ancestry usually CONTAINS the orchestrator's unpushed harvest commits. Branch deletion + jj import treats bookmark-less ancestry as garbage.

**It fires WITHOUT manual deletion (second incident, same day):** the Claude Code harness auto-removes a dead/finished agent's *unchanged* worktree — including its branch. A phase agent that died before committing had its worktree auto-cleaned, and the next jj import abandoned the (recovered!) 4-commit chain a second time. @ was empty so it rebased cleanly onto main — no (conflict) markers, the only symptoms were @ sitting directly on main and the chain's files missing from disk.

**How to apply:**
- Keep a local bookmark (e.g. `trackb`) on the unpushed chain tip AT ALL TIMES while worktree agents are in flight — move it after every harvest. This is a precondition for dispatching worktree agents, not just for manual cleanup. (The bookmark exports to a git branch, making the chain import-reachable.)
- Never delete an agent worktree branch while unpushed harvest commits exist below @; defer manual cleanup to after the release push.
- Immediately after ANY git ref surgery or agent-worktree disappearance in this repo, run `jj log` (graph form, never a flat template — the flat view hid both this and an earlier false alarm) and look for (conflict) markers, vanished commits, and @ parenting directly off main.
- Recovery, preferred: git objects survive until GC — `jj new <hidden-tip-sha>` revives the exact chain (jj un-hides the ancestry; no cherry-picking), then bookmark it. Fallback if revival divergence bites: `git cat-file -e <sha>` each, `jj abandon` conflicted copies, `jj new <main>`, re-`git cherry-pick -n` + `jj commit` in order.

Related: [[claude-pool-project]], [[jj-config-relative-path-cwd]]
